description: Most backend services validate a Google ID token themselves, server-side, on every request — no session state, no cookies, just a Bearer token checked against Google's public keys. [[posts-api|posts-api]] and [[daily-api|daily-api]] verify it with google-auth and then require the caller's email to be in an ALLOWED_WRITERS allowlist. Some services, such as [[ideas-api|ideas-api]] and [[history-api|history-api]], use Azure's EasyAuth for token validation at the platform level, which reduces application code but requires configuration in Azure. Machine authentication via custom headers is supported for specific bot-driven workflows in APIs like [[ideas-api|ideas-api]] and [[history-api|history-api]], and should be implemented thoughtfully and documented clearly.

sections.content: [[ideas-api|ideas-api]], [[dashboard-api|dashboard-api]], and [[history-api|history-api]] rely on Azure Functions' built-in EasyAuth: Azure validates the Google ID token at the platform layer before the request ever reaches application code, then injects the validated identity as a request header. dashboard-api decodes the same X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL header the identical way ideas-api does. This approach reduces the amount of authentication code in the application itself but requires configuration in Azure Function App settings, which can complicate future migrations or debugging. Additionally, both [[ideas-api|ideas-api]] and [[history-api|history-api]] support machine authentication via custom headers (e.g., X-Ideas-Key for [[ideas-api|ideas-api]] and HISTORY_WRITE_KEY for [[history-api|history-api]]) to enable bot-driven workflows alongside user-based authentication. Recent updates to [[ideas-api|ideas-api]] now allow machine-key authentication for creating projects (POST /projects), aligning it with other write endpoints like ideas and updates.
sections.heading: Azure EasyAuth (platform-level)

sections.content: [[posts-api|posts-api]] and [[daily-api|daily-api]] verify the Google ID token in application code with google-auth (audience = the configured GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID values), then check the caller's email against an ALLOWED_WRITERS allowlist; daily-api also partitions every table by that verified email, so each user only sees their own rows. [[learning-plan-api|learning-plan-api]] also verifies Google ID tokens server-side, and [[running-app|running-app]] validates them against Google's tokeninfo endpoint. None of these use Azure EasyAuth.
sections.heading: Application-level Google ID token

summary: How user and machine identity is verified across the system: mostly server-side Google ID token validation, with Azure EasyAuth exceptions and machine key support for specific APIs.
title: Authentication
